people.label: P1
people.zygosity_or_genotype: compound heterozygous (stated; confirmed by parental Sanger testing)
people.key_phenotypes: recurrent severe infections from the neonatal period (bacterial meningitis at 1.5 months, Candida and Gram-negative infections); recurrent ecthyma gangrenosum; marked leukocytosis up to 100,000/mm3; severe growth retardation; periodontitis

quotes.quote: We report the case of a 3-year-and-8-month-old female (P1) born to non- consanguineous parents, with a significant family history of LAD.

Genetic analysis revealed a compound heterozygous genotype: a frameshift deletion c.119_128del (p.Gly40AlafsTer7) inherited from the father, and a novel missense variant c.700G>A (p.Glu234Lys) inherited from the mother.
At 1½ months, she developed bacterial meningitis (pleocytosis 200 cells/mm³, 88% neutrophils), although no causative organism was identified.
Recurrent skin infections (Figure 1), particularly ecthyma gangrenosum involving the buttocks, became a prominent feature of her clinical course.
All episodes were accompanied by marked leukocytosis, reaching 100,000 WBC/mm³.
Severe growth retardation and periodontitis were also present.
| father | ITGB2 | Chr21:46330218 | c.119_128del | p.Gly40AlafsTer7 | Pathogenic | Heterozygous |
inherited from her healthy father

phenotype_specificity.statement: 42625796: P1 had features the authors call classic for LAD I (neonatal-onset severe recurrent infections, ecthyma gangrenosum, marked leukocytosis, growth retardation, periodontitis) and a family history of LAD; genome sequencing found no other variants of note in inborn-error-of-immunity genes. CD18 expression was normal, which the authors call atypical.

quotes.quote: This clinical and biological presentation, together with her family history, was unambiguously suggestive of a leukocyte adhesion defect.
Analysis of genes associated with inborn errors of immunity did not identify any additional variants of potential clinical significance beyond those reported here.

Immunological evaluation revealed normal lymphocyte immunophenotyping with normal surface expression of adhesion molecules confirmed in two independent experiments (LFA-1: 99.5%, CD18: 99.5%) (Table 1, Figure 2).
Her sister (P2) died at 17 days of age from severe sepsis with marked hyperleukocytosis (138,000 WBC/mm³) and delayed umbilical cord separation.
Additionally, a heterozygous variant in ALG2 (c.1055_1056del, p.Ser352TyrfsTer2) was identified, classified as likely pathogenic according to ACMG criteria.
The elevated absolute T-cell counts observed in both affected siblings may reflect altered lymphocyte trafficking secondary to impaired β2-integrin function.
| CD18 expression | 99.5 | 96 |

segregation.statement: 42625796: the healthy father is heterozygous for the deletion; the healthy mother carries the other allele. The affected sister P2 is described but her genotype is not stated explicitly. 22134107: no segregation data.

quotes.quote: Familial segregation analysis by Sanger sequencing of the ITGB2 gene confirmed compound heterozygosity, with paternal transmission of the pathogenic c.119_128del variant and maternal transmission of the c.700G>A missense variant (Table 2).
| father | ITGB2 | Chr21:46330218 | c.119_128del | p.Gly40AlafsTer7 | Pathogenic | Heterozygous |

Genetic testing identified two variants in ITGB2: a pathogenic deletion (c.119_128del) inherited from her healthy father and a missense variant (c.700G>A), classified as likely pathogenic, inherited from her healthy mother.

In our study, CD11a expression was preserved in both patients (P1 and P2) despite the presence of the ITGB2 deletion, suggesting a more complex relationship between genotype and surface integrin expression.

functional.statement: No assay of this variant in this batch. 42625796: P1 (compound heterozygous) had normal CD18 (99.5%) and LFA-1 on lymphocytes in two experiments and a normal NBT test; the authors note, citing Smith et al., that the deletion was reported with absent CD18 in homozygous form. 22134107 types the row LAD-I^o (< 5% CD18).

quotes.quote: Immunological evaluation revealed normal lymphocyte immunophenotyping with normal surface expression of adhesion molecules confirmed in two independent experiments (LFA-1: 99.5%, CD18: 99.5%) (Table 1, Figure 2).
The nitroblue tetrazolium (NBT) test was normal, indicating preserved neutrophil oxidative burst activity.
Importantly, this deletion has been previously reported in homozygous form as causative of severe LAD I and has been associated with complete absence of CD18 expression (13).
As highlighted by Smith et al., among three patients carrying this deletion, only one exhibited CD18 expression of approximately 50%, while showing an absence of CD11a.

In our study, CD11a expression was preserved in both patients (P1 and P2) despite the presence of the ITGB2 deletion, suggesting a more complex relationship between genotype and surface integrin expression.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Frameshift deletion of 10 nt in exon 3 (exon 3 spans c.59-c.147 by the intron positions in 22134107), p.(Gly40AlafsTer7), from the batch HGVS. 42625796 states it predicts truncation and complete loss of CD18 function. The paper describes LAD-I as autosomal recessive and caused by decreased expression or function of CD18 (beta-2 integrin).

quotes.quote: The 10-nucleotide deletion leads to a frameshift and a premature stop codon at position 7 downstream.
The predicted consequence is truncation of the β2 integrin protein.
The c.119_128del variant results in a frameshift with a premature termination codon, predicting a complete loss of CD18 function.
intron 3 c.147_148; intron 4 c.328_329; intron 5 c.499_500; intron 6 c.741_742;
Leukocyte adhesion deficiency (LAD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by decreased expression or functioning of CD18, the β_2 subunit of the leukocyte β_2 integrins [1].

computational_predictions.statement: 42625796: in-silico tools support a deleterious effect (CADD > 30, MutationTaster 'disease causing').

quotes.quote: In silico prediction tools support a deleterious effect (CADD >30, MutationTaster: disease causing) (11, 12).

concerns: 22134107 is a mutation-database update: the variant appears only as a Table 1 row with an accession number, with no case description, sex, clinical phenotype, zygosity or parental testing. (Applies to the five accessions A0018, A0068, A0083, A0089, A0133.)

Carrier possibly missing from the batch: P1's sister P2 (affected, died at 17 days, delayed cord separation) has immunophenotyping in Table 1 of 42625796, and the Discussion speaks of 'the presence of the ITGB2 deletion' in both P1 and P2 and of 'both affected siblings', but P2's genotype is never stated explicitly.
A maternal cousin of P1 had LAD-I with absent CD18 (and a maternal uncle died with delayed cord separation); their genotypes are not reported. Note c.119_128del is the paternal allele in P1.
Another candidate variant in P1: the ITGB2 c.700G>A p.(Glu234Lys) other allele, and a heterozygous ALG2 c.1055_1056del (recessive conditions; authors consider heterozygosity alone not causal).

42625796 Table 2 gives the same genomic position 'Chr21:46330218' for all three family-member rows, including c.700G>A, whose supplement gives hg19 chr21:g.46,321,448; the table position likely belongs to the deletion only.

42625796's data-availability statement gives an NCBI accession SCV007539359 (an SCV-type accession); the coordinator may want to check whether this family's variants have already been deposited, which would affect this candidate's gap status.

Contradiction in kind: 22134107 types the deletion row LAD-I^o and 42625796 cites absent CD18 in homozygotes, yet P1 (compound heterozygous) has normal CD18 expression; the authors attribute this to the missense allele.

42625796 mentions CRISPR correction of 'a 10-bp deletion in exon 3 of ITGB2' in patient-derived cells (ref 17); the paper does not say it is c.119_128del, so it is not counted as functional evidence here.
The 22134107 row cites refs [3, 20, 25, 26] plus Unpubl.; those papers are not in this batch.
22134107 numbers cDNA from the A of the ATG (+1), which matches the batch numbering; it names no RefSeq transcript (it mentions GenBank M15395 only for the offset).
notes_for_panel: Recurrent deletion: 5 families in 22134107 (both alleles counted, presumed homozygous in at least one) plus one compound heterozygous girl with parental phase in 42625796. 42625796 itself classifies the deletion (see authors_classification).
